items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green, creamery 1891 (Story 1). Gideon Vose not named in Section A; core fact credited under list-type rule.
Article VII: payment by butterfat test at the delivery station, not by milk weight.
'Under payment by weight, nothing that followed would have cost anyone a dollar.'
Loomis, Teague, Sill not in Section A.
Section A calls Selby Vose 'the Association's manager' only; son/1913 absent (B3 gives 1911, not creditable here).
Station-gain ledger line not in Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up valley, opened 4 May 1896, borrowing of Larrow Green.
Weighing, test, cream hauled to Larrow Green, skim returned; short charge in test bottle read proportionally short (Story 8). Composite sample not mentioned; core credited.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, own glass came up 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, $77.93. (Later 'five dozen' in Story 6 is taken as a deduction.)
Flat 0.19 in every month of the year, June and February alike (Story 2).
No statement that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, none in the county.
Keddie tester from the 1896 opening; dismissed 30 April 1925.
Bench routine and the test book's columns/one-hand keeping not described.
No 1896 3.80 figure; run says 'From the station's opening, milk tested there ran low', contradicting the step at the change of glass.
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, tests markedly higher, back to 3.61, question mark. 3.80 not stated; core credited.
Married to Orra, 'Orra's brother Emmet Brant'.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) absent; both required.
Died February 1934 with the imputation on him.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom. Brant's being largest not stated; core credited.
Weigh book dated 1 January 1900 (planted); scales agreeing not stated.
Conflates the gaps: gives Larrow Green 3.78 vs 3.61 and calls the shortfall 0.19 'lower than the valley baseline' (Story 2, C1b, G).
Grigg committee sampled Jan-Mar 1908, hay finding reported as its opinion, not asserted.
Brant's 1910 figures and proportional loss not in Section A.
Roy Brant 1929 / lent to Ivy 1958 absent.
No Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd; only 'Alder Corners cheese factory across the ridge'.
Four Hessel Bottom farmers hauled there in summer. 1915 absent; core credited.
Independence not stated with two of the four elements.
Same four men's milk 3.80 at Alder Corners vs 3.61 at Ostrey Hollow.
Same milk tested differently proves milk good: 'Not theft, not fraud, not feed'.
Rosalie as Jerome's daughter and her 1958 copying absent; run has her doing the testing.
Strawn named, kin to no one, but 1907-1936 span absent from Section A.
Lactometer never finding water not in Section A.
June 1923, burette, condemned the entire lot (day not given).
Says he drew no inference, but not that he wrote no figure / no report beyond condemnation.
1924 average given as 3.85.
Crate to loft present; notebooks to college library in 1947 absent.
Petition January 1925.
Board under Alonzo Frick, three sittings, two in the station weigh room.
Watering, cream theft, wet hay argued; no cause established.
Four books listed, but not that Strawn's notebook contained the answer and was read for other lines.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, four days before $3,800 'without admission' award; no cause found.
Loss given as $19,600; no one-fifth of $19,000, no charging to the station-gain account.
Granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College, with Vaught.
Assembly of records never in one room not described.
February 1958, loft over intake room, nine pipettes.
Mean delivery 16.27 c.c., 1.33 short, 7.56% low.
Seven-percent error, not 95 percent of true / 3.80.
67,000 lb and $19,600; no 40M/76,000/ledger identity.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 24 years after death, crate 35 years in loft.
Granddaughter.
Duncan is Ansel's son and Ivy's father.
Second cousins via Roy and Duncan as first cousins.
Full vs half siblings question not raised or declined.
Gideon Vose, son not nephew.
Significance given as ledger-signing habit, not Article VII / Vose Jerseys.
Verdict sentence: 'Cannot be determined from the sources with certainty.'
One hearsay claim vs one denial; no documented relationship.
True 3.906, gap 0.296 (NT-1 cascade).
1,440,000 (arithmetic error; key 1,444,000).
72 pipettes but 1.33 c.c. short, not 0.88.
'26 years, 1 month', not 26 years 6 weeks / 1 month 11 days.
Asserts ~1,100,000 lb (abstention item A02).
Variable: the measuring glass; only the glass differed.
Herds, season, tester, machinery, pasture held constant.
'Markedly higher', no 3.80 figure.
Cause in glass, not watering/theft; limit: exact magnitude not established.
1911 interval, Alder Corners book, Brant weigh book.
Independence argued; 1911 reason 'requires no post-1958 knowledge'.
Asserts 'No' - Teague never questioned (A09).
Declines the literal question ('cannot definitively establish prior knowledge'), confusing it with A03.
Only two of five (ledger signing, 1919 circular); manager date given as 1911.
Declares sources do not establish what he knew; no statement by Vose survives; signature-without-reading.
Granddaughter vs great-niece, 1897 vs 1898 glass, nine vs eleven families, $3,800 vs $3,500 - each resolved with method (cap 3). Invoice left unresolved.
Explicitly reports no near-tie pairs.
A04, A06, A10 not identified as unsettleable.
States no self-contradictions found.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and Alder Corners 3.80.
Theft defeated by 1911 interval with same man at bench.
Bog hay (Grigg 1908) defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter, nothing in summer.
Asserts 'No' - board never examined the glassware (A07).
Asserts Keddie believed the cause was the glass (A05).
About 129 words.
At most two record series (arbitration, 1958 measurement).
$19,600 and 16.27 stated.
1897, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy named.
